scope: Prieto Diaz, Sorsogon coastal biodiversity evidence from a 2022 fish eDNA survey. This is not a freshwater-river inventory, capture checklist, or species-by-site occurrence table.

study.article: Application of eDNA metabarcoding in the assessment of fish biodiversity in Philippine mangroves: Challenges and opportunities
study.publication: Regional Studies in Marine Science 77 (2024), article 103642; published 2024-12-10.
studySites: Bongabong, Roxas and Mansalay, Oriental Mindoro (West Philippine Sea)
study.fieldWindow: July-August 2022; one high-tide water-sampling campaign reported.
study.method: 12S eDNA metabarcoding from water. The article reports 19 sites overall: 10 Prieto Diaz site codes (PDS1-PDS10) and nine Oriental Mindoro site codes (OMS1-OMS9). Site types include mangrove-recolonized fishponds, natural mangroves, mangrove plantations, seagrass, coral reef and open sea.
study.reportedOverallResults: The article reports 168 fish MOTUs, 89 species and 44 families across both regions. These are combined study totals, not Sorsogon-only counts.
study.dataAvailability: The article says data will be made available on request; no public dataset or site-by-taxon sequence/read table was found in the reviewed material.
study.articleLicense: Crossref metadata identifies the version of record as CC BY-NC-ND 4.0. No Bangwit publication or derivative-data approval is inferred.

siteEvidence.coordinatePrecision: The reviewed article text gives a municipality-level reference coordinate, not an independently verified coordinate for each PDS sample. Do not assign all detections to that point or to an unverified waterbody polygon.
siteEvidence.habitatInterpretation: The table reports saline water measurements during sampling. Site-type labels and these single-visit values do not establish a permanent salinity class or a freshwater river reach.

correction.title: Corrigendum to Application of eDNA metabarcoding in the assessment of fish biodiversity in Philippine mangroves: Challenges and opportunities
correction.publication: Regional Studies in Marine Science 91 (2025), article 104565; Crossref identifies it as a publisher-issued erratum/update to the 2024 article.
correction.status: Existence and DOI were verified through Crossref and the UP Diliman Institute of Biology publication list. The correction text itself was not retrieved; publisher page access was blocked in this review.
correction.decision: Do not use the article's total or any taxon-level claim as a current corrected result until the corrigendum is obtained and its scope is checked.

qualityAndUseLimits: eDNA detection is environmental DNA evidence, not a captured, photographed or physically vouchered individual; transport and persistence can complicate local-presence interpretation.
The article reports site types and combined regional species results, but the reviewed material does not provide an independently verified species-by-PDS-code matrix or public read-count data.
The authors discuss incomplete Philippine reference databases and possible cross-contamination, so taxonomic assignments and isolated site detections require source-level review.
Do not convert the Prieto Diaz municipality-level coordinate into sample coordinates or river/lake geometry.
This coastal eDNA dataset is distinct from the already registered 2026 Amihan-monsoon eDNA study; do not merge the studies or their detections.
nextActions: Obtain and inspect the publisher corrigendum and corrected article version before transcribing any species claims.
Check whether the authors or a public repository can provide the sample-to-MOTU/species crosswalk, sequence accessions, and site coordinates together with reuse terms; no request has been sent.
Continue Sorsogon freshwater river/lake and coastal-source reviews as separate habitat and evidence classes.
